[https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-research-tools/r-part-I](https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-research-tools/r-part-I)

**Welcome!** This workshop is intended to provide learners with an **introduction to R and RStudio**. Through hands-on exercises, you will learn how to **navigate the RStudio interface** and **use basic R programming skills** to work efficiently with your data. We will also learn how to **create and manipulate objects**, execute code, use functions with arguments, and access information stored in data frames within the R environment.

### Who are these materials for?

- **Educators** in higher education with or without familiarity with open research planning to **teach open research novices**
- **Self-learners** with no or limited familiarity with open research planning to **develop and build** up on their open research skills

## Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;">
| Prerequisite   |  Description  | Where to find it   |
|------------|------------|------------|
| RStudio installed | Version 2026.04.0+526 or higher | [Download](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) |
| R installed | Version 4.6.0 or higher | [Download](https://www.r-project.org/) |
| Accessibility sheet for computers | Fundamentals of computer literacy | [Download here ](assets/Accessibility_sheet_for_computers_OSSS26.pdf)
</div>

## Learning goals

At the end of this session, you or your learners will be able to ...

- **Navigate** the RStudio interface (Console, Environment, Script, and Output panes).
- **Differentiate** between basic data types in R (numeric, character, logical, integer) and how they are used.
- **Execute** operations in the Console and R Script using appropriate operators.
- **Assign** and **re-assign** values, vectors, and lists to objects. 
- **Specify** arguments within functions to modify how the function produces its output.
-**Index** dataframes to access and retrieve specific information.
